contract: the operations of ass-parse-scripts, ass-parse-chunks and ass-parse-events whose libass result differs by target, one fixture each, recorded as those features record them. The reference flags every conversion from double to int whose result C leaves to the target out of range or for NaN, by an explicit check where libass makes it: a drawing coordinate in 26.6 (double_to_d6, lrint narrowed from long to int), \pbo copied into a drawing glyph, an animated \clip or \iclip, \fade's alpha (interpolate_alpha) and the delay of a Banner or Scroll effect, and a drawing coordinate landing on INT_MIN, whose abs libass's bound check takes. Reads of values that go through C long beyond int, an event time read with sscanf's %d and a Matroska packet's ReadOrder read with atoi, differ by target without a flag

each case is pinned per target from that target's own reference run, with the reference's flag; a case passes when the candidate, the reference and the target's pin agree, and a target a case has no pin for runs and reports it without comparing

long-width behaviour follows each target's libass; every double-to-int conversion out of range follows libass on 32-bit ARM with GCC: it saturates at int's range and NaN converts to 0, so an out-of-range drawing coordinate is rejected and a NaN one is 0. Two kinds of case have declared deviations: on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, drawings-infinite and drawings-int-min, whose coordinates libass converts with a 64-bit long there, and on both targets drawings-int-min-x and drawings-int-min-y, a coordinate landing exactly on INT_MIN, which the crate rejects and libass built with GCC accepts
the file is read, its directives and commands parsed and the script or stream read before each timed and memory operation, and the reference's library, renderer and track are created once, outside it

open_deviations.reading: A drawing coordinate outside the signed 26.6 range discards the drawing
open_deviations.clause: ISO C sections 6.3.1.3 and 7.12.9.5 leave out-of-range signed narrowing or rounding dependent on the implementation. The drawing contract uses fixed 32-bit bounds
open_deviations.candidate: Rejects the drawing for the extreme coordinate in each case.
open_deviations.reference: The AArch64 build rounds using a 64-bit long and keeps low 32 bits, admitting the resulting drawing.

open_deviations.reading: The minimum signed coordinate is outside the admissible drawing bound
open_deviations.clause: ISO C section 7.22.6.1 paragraph 2 leaves abs of an unrepresentable result undefined
open_deviations.candidate: Rejects the drawing with an INT_MIN coordinate in either axis.
open_deviations.reference: Both named target builds admit the drawing with an INT_MIN coordinate.
